dedupe_keys.name: food access impact survey for harris county and southeast texas after hurricane harvey 2017 food retailer and food aid agency data designsafe prj 2769

description: This DesignSafe dataset records how Hurricane Harvey in 2017 disrupted the supply side of food access in Harris County and Southeast Texas. A Texas research team surveyed a random sample of food retailers in person in Harris, Jefferson and Orange counties, 210 completed surveys, and 32 food aid agencies online, five to eight months after the storm. The surveys cover damage to people, property and products, disruption of transportation, water, electricity, buildings and communications, and how long each store was closed, ran reduced hours or went without fresh food. The team found that infrastructure failures, especially transportation and electricity, cut food access, and that impacts on staff also mattered. The retailer and agency data, survey instruments, methods report and replication code are free to download from the DesignSafe Data Depot, each with its own DOI, and a related article appeared in the Journal of the American Planning Association. Coverage is three Texas counties after one hurricane. Caveats: the data are anonymised, so store locations are not given; the licence is shown only on the DesignSafe page; sample sizes are modest. Simulation uses: restoration times for food retail and dependencies of food access on power and roads in hurricane recovery models. Related records: the post-hurricane supply chain case study (case_study-post-hurricane-supply-chains-harvey-irma-maria) covers the same storm at the level of national supply chains, and the USDA Food Access Research Atlas (data-usda-ers-food-access-research-atlas) gives baseline access.
